Query Snowflake as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__snowflake.R
oauth_db_snowflake.Rd

Query Snowflake with the visitor's account and role using DBI or dbplyr. Set the warehouse, database, and schema for your queries, or use the account's defaults.

Usage

oauth_db_snowflake(
  authorization,
  server,
  database = NULL,
  schema = NULL,
  warehouse = NULL,
  role,
  ...,
  required_scopes = paste0("session:role:", role),
  target = NULL,
  driver = "SnowflakeDSIIDriver",
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

server

Database hostname.

database, schema, warehouse

Optional connection settings. NULL uses the driver's or account's defaults.

role

Snowflake role for this connection.

...

Named Snowflake ODBC connection options.

required_scopes

Permissions to check before use. The default is the Snowflake role scope, paste0("session:role:", role). For External OAuth, supply the scope names configured by the integration.

target

Named shinyOAuth token target, or NULL for the default token.

driver

Installed ODBC driver name.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning an odbc DBI connection.

Details

Install odbc and the Snowflake ODBC driver. Use oauth_db_snowflake_client() for Snowflake's own OAuth integration, or a shinyOAuth client configured for your External OAuth provider.

Create con inside server() and get connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression before querying. The helper opens the connection on first use and closes it when the authorization or session ends.

For names containing ODBC delimiters, use odbc::quote_value().

See also

oauth_db_snowflake_client(). vignette("snowflake", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_snowflake(
  auth$connection,
  server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
  role = "REPORTING_READER",
  warehouse = "REPORTING_WH",
  database = "ANALYTICS"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE()")
})
} # }
